business_problem: Cornell needed a more robust and standardized maintenance platform because paper-based tickets, uneven mobile access, and disconnected processes made it hard to coordinate facilities work, track compliance, and plan preventative maintenance across a large campus.
solution_summary: Cornell University expanded its use of IBM Maximo Application Suite from a basic work-delivery system into a broader facilities-operations platform for campus maintenance. Working with IBM consulting support, the university reimplemented the latest Maximo environment, integrated legacy systems, standardized asset and job-plan definitions, and extended the platform with a mobile experience that let more staff capture work, labor, materials, and asset-condition data in the field. The design supports preventative maintenance, corrective maintenance, compliance work, inspections, and forecasting in one system rather than through paper tickets and separate tools. Maximo became the shared record for buildings, systems, work orders, and reporting, while mobile access and offline use helped technicians respond in real time and keep work moving during the pandemic. The result is a paperless maintenance operating model that improves resource allocation, compliance tracking, and decision-making across Cornell's extensive facilities footprint.

solution_components.name: IBM Maximo Application Suite
solution_components.role: Serves as Cornell's shared platform for maintenance work orders, preventative-maintenance planning, inspections, reporting, and mobile field operations.

data_flow: Work requests, labor updates, materials usage, inspections, and asset-condition details are entered into Maximo from desktop and mobile workflows, then used for scheduling, compliance reporting, backlog management, and preventative-maintenance forecasting across campus facilities.
business_outcome: Cornell moved to a paperless, more mobile maintenance operation that handles higher request volumes, cuts support overhead, improves compliance reporting, and gives campus teams the data they need to allocate resources and plan maintenance more effectively.
architecture_clues: The new mobile solution is an extension of Maximo rather than a separate database.
Cornell standardized asset naming and job-plan granularity as part of the reimplementation.
The university plans to integrate a new building automation system more fully and expand predictive-maintenance use cases.

With IBM's consulting help, the Cornell team integrated legacy systems into Maximo's latest version alongside the new mobile solution that would enable more users.
